source.title: Strong convexity-guided hyper-parameter optimization for flatter losses

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied; no truncation or garbling apparent.
record.tranche_reason: The paper measures a sharpness-related quantity and reports test performance for selected hyperparameter configurations, bearing on the proposed relation between flatness and generalization, but does not directly measure the versions' stated conditions or gap measures.
record.gate_note: The paper's own results are hyperparameter-search performance comparisons, not direct tests of memorization/generalization coexistence, width beyond interpolation, architecture comparisons, optimizer or batch-size effects, dropout effects, magnitude-aware sharpness ranking, or removal of memorized examples. Figure 1 describes two Australian-dataset configurations with different strong-convexity values and generalization errors, but does not report their numeric test metrics in the supplied text. The paper also cites prior findings on flatness and generalization; those cited results are not its own rows.
record.test_reason: The study uses an assumed flatness–generalization relationship to design hyperparameter search and evaluates search performance and runtime. Its strong-convexity proxy and Australian configuration comparison do not test V7's magnitude-aware perturbation measure or its ranking of generalization gaps. No own results test V1–V6 or V8.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially accurate. The authors conclude that their strong-convexity-guided search finds good configurations using 10 full training runs after inexpensive screening, demonstrated on 12 tabular and two image datasets. They report 13%–33% of competing methods' runtime on the vehicle dataset and motivate the approach through a proposed connection between strong convexity, flatness, and generalization.
record.recipe_differences: A hyperparameter-optimization study using one-epoch strong-convexity estimates to select configurations; it does not reproduce the claim versions' interventions or comparisons.
record.method_sensitivity: The authors describe two Australian-dataset configurations with different strong-convexity values and generalization outcomes; hyperparameters are varied in the search, including batch size and dropout rates in the stated search spaces, but condition-specific generalization results are not reported.

fits_no_version.finding: Figure 1 and the Introduction compare Australian-dataset configurations with strong-convexity values 0.112 and 1.133. The authors report smaller accuracy and AUC generalization gaps for the former; the latter reaches perfect training accuracy and AUC but performs worse on the test set. Numeric test metrics are unavailable in the supplied text.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A lower Hessian-based strong-convexity proxy can accompany smaller generalization gaps across neural-network hyperparameter configurations on tabular classification.

record.problems: Figure 1's described comparison lacks numeric test metrics in the supplied text. The paper reports aggregate HPO benchmark medians rather than direct tests of the listed claim versions.
record.rows_left_out: No rows meet the criteria: Table 1 reports performance of HPO methods, not an outcome of the claim's object itself; Figure 1's configuration comparison is only described qualitatively and does not state a numeric or explicit test-error value. Related-work results are cited prior work and excluded.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting versus natural-label held-out performance under the same architecture and training recipe.
Test-error trends as width increases beyond zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under specified tuning budgets and recovery strategies.
Large versus small batches at fixed epoch budgets and recipe changes that mitigate penalties.
Dropout versus no dropout and dependence on data size, dropout strength, or augmentation.
Magnitude-aware weight-perturbation tolerance versus generalization gaps among convolutional networks with similarly low training loss, including ranking against norm and margin measures.
Retraining after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: Correct the record's tests/T2 classification to uses_without_test/T4. Figure 1 supplies an explicit qualitative result despite missing numeric test metrics; its exclusion from V7 rests on the different measure and comparison, not on the absence of numbers. Table 1 compares HPO methods rather than isolating any listed claim's effect. The omitted Figure 1 result is already declared in rows_left_out, so it requires no missing entry.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label test performance under the same architecture and recipe are not compared.
No width sweep beyond zero training error or test-error trend by width is reported.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison is reported.
No adaptive optimizer versus SGD held-out comparison is reported.
No large- versus small-batch comparison at fixed epoch budgets is reported.
Dropout is among searched hyperparameters for SVHN, but the paper reports no separate dropout condition/result.
The paper does not test magnitude-aware sharpness or rank generalization gaps across networks with similar training loss.
No memorized-example identification, removal, or retraining comparison is reported.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
